title: Exponential flattening rank can coexist with compact exact contraction
summary: A useful result for representation design: low ordinary tensor rank is only one compression mechanism. Look for a compact algebraic class closed under the operations the algorithm needs.
content: For invertible d-by-d L, the Gaussian boundary tensor defined by principal Pfaffians of [[0,L],[-L^T,0]] has flattening rank 2^d but an O(d^2)-entry description. Exterior powers of L prove the rank. When the internal skew block C is invertible, the entire boundary contracts to Pf(C) times the Gaussian tensor with matrix E+D^T C^(-1)D, using polynomial field arithmetic.
whenToUse: A useful result for representation design: low ordinary tensor rank is only one compression mechanism. Look for a compact algebraic class closed under the operations the algorithm needs.
limitations: The prototype's Schur chart requires invertible even-dimensional C. Singular C returns UNSUPPORTED, not zero; a complete implementation needs chart changes. Generic ordinary crossings violate Gaussian closure in the specified ordering and basis.
